data.label: Detect New Opportunity
data.description: Trigger when a new sales opportunity is created in the CRM.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on a CRM record creation event. No AI, ML, or language understanding is required. L0 is sufficient.
data.errorHandling: If the webhook payload is malformed or missing the opportunity id, acknowledge the event, log the failure, and stop processing. Retry webhook delivery once if the source supports retries.

data.label: Validate Required Fields
data.description: Check that the opportunity has an assigned owner, a dollar value, and a target close date.
data.rationale: This is pure rule-based validation of required fields. The logic is fully deterministic: presence/absence checks and type/format checks. L0 is appropriate.
conditions: target_close_date is present and valid date
data.errorHandling: On validation failure, collect all missing/invalid fields, write a validation error record, and route to correction handling. Do not proceed to scoring.

data.label: Handle Missing Data
data.description: Route invalid opportunities for correction when required fields are missing.
data.rationale: This step routes records based on a validation outcome. It is deterministic workflow control with no learning or language generation. L0 is sufficient.
data.errorHandling: Persist the validation issues, mark the opportunity as blocked, and notify the owner or source system. If persistence fails, retry with exponential backoff and then enqueue for manual review.

data.label: Analyze Similar Deals
data.description: Compare the opportunity against historical win-rate data for similar deals.
data.rationale: This step compares the opportunity to historical win-rate data and likely relies on a predictive scoring model or statistical classifier/regressor. L0 can query data, but it cannot infer similarity-based win likelihood well. Since the task is structured prediction rather than language understanding, L1 is appropriate.
data.errorHandling: If the historical dataset or feature vector is unavailable, fall back to a baseline score derived from segment-level averages and log a model-quality warning. If the model execution fails, retry once and then use fallback heuristics.

data.label: Assign Confidence Score
data.description: Generate a deal-stage confidence score based on historical comparison results.
data.rationale: This is a numeric scoring or regression-style output derived from structured historical signals. It does not require language generation. L1 is justified because the score is probabilistic and learned or model-based rather than simple fixed rules.
data.errorHandling: Clamp invalid scores to a safe range, emit a model output error, and fall back to a conservative confidence estimate if the predicted value is missing or non-numeric.

data.label: Evaluate Proposal Prep Criteria
data.description: Check whether the deal is high-confidence and above 50000 dollars.
data.rationale: This is a straightforward deterministic threshold check on two values. No uncertainty handling beyond boolean comparison is needed. L0 is appropriate.
data.errorHandling: If inputs are missing or non-numeric, skip automation for this branch and log a threshold evaluation error. Continue to stale-opportunity evaluation when safe.

data.label: Schedule Proposal Prep Meeting
data.description: Automatically schedule a proposal-prep meeting with the sales engineering team for qualifying deals.
data.rationale: This action requires interacting with an external scheduling/calendar or CRM integration to create the meeting. That makes it tool-augmented rather than purely deterministic. A single agent could decide the action and call the scheduling API, so L4 is appropriate.
data.errorHandling: If scheduling fails due to conflict or API error, retry up to 2 times, then create a task for manual scheduling and notify the owner. Preserve idempotency by checking for an existing meeting before creation.

data.label: Detect Stalled Opportunity
data.description: Check whether the opportunity has stalled for more than 14 days without activity.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic date/elapsed-time comparison against an activity timestamp. It is a simple rule check with no learning or language requirements. L0 is sufficient.
data.errorHandling: If last activity is missing, treat the opportunity as stale only when the record has no activity history; otherwise log the anomaly and route to manual review. Retry timestamp lookup if the activity store is temporarily unavailable.

data.label: Flag Manager Review
data.description: Flag stalled opportunities for sales manager review.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic workflow action that sets a flag or status for escalation. It does not require AI or external reasoning. L0 is appropriate.
data.errorHandling: If flag update fails, retry once and then create an escalation task in the CRM with the failure details.

data.label: Draft Re-engagement Email
data.description: Create a re-engagement email draft for the rep to send.
data.rationale: Drafting an email requires language generation. A single LLM call can produce the message from the opportunity context without external tool use. L3 is sufficient because this is self-contained generation, not multi-agent collaboration.
data.errorHandling: If generation fails, fall back to a short template-based draft and log the LLM error. Ensure the output contains subject, body, and call-to-action fields.

data.label: Record Stage Transition
data.description: Log every stage transition with timestamp and triggering event.
data.rationale: This is deterministic logging/auditing of events with timestamps and metadata. No AI is needed. L0 is appropriate.
data.errorHandling: Write transition logs transactionally. If logging fails, retry the write and queue the event for later replay to avoid losing audit history.

data.label: Complete Workflow
data.description: Finish processing after validations, scoring, automation, and logging are complete.
data.rationale: This is a terminal workflow node with no computation or reasoning. It simply ends the process, so L0 applies.
conditions: all required branch actions completed or safely skipped
data.errorHandling: No action required; if reached after a recoverable failure, ensure failure details were already logged before termination.

data.condition: owner_id present and amount > 0 and target_close_date valid
data.label: if valid

data.condition: owner_id missing or amount missing/invalid or target_close_date missing/invalid
data.label: if invalid
if not stalled, log no-action transition

message: This workflow now includes deterministic validation, predictive scoring, conditional automation for high-value high-confidence deals, a stale-opportunity escalation path, and audit logging. Tool bindings were added per step using CRM, calendar, database, validation, ML, and LLM integrations. Error paths include invalid-field handling, model fallback behavior, API retry logic, and safe logging/replay for audit durability. Parallel paths were preserved and refined so automation branches can write stage-transition logs concurrently while the core workflow remains idempotent and traceable.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a new sales opportunity is created in the CRM, verify that the deal has an assigned owner, a stated dollar value, and a target close date. Check the opportunity against historical win-rate data for similar deals and assign a deal-stage confidence score. For high-confidence deals above 50000 dollars, automatically schedule a proposal-prep meeting with the sales engineering team. For deals that have stalled more than 14 days without activity, flag the opportunity for sales manager review and draft a re-engagement email for the rep. Record every stage transition with timestamp and triggering event.
